mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy environment that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with consecutive FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in federal funds rate and unemployment rate signals coordinated monetary easing and labor market strength that boosts corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with concurrent FEDFUNDS and UNRATE declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes characterized by strong housing starts and GDP growth, S&P 500 forward returns turn positive as consumer demand sustains corporate earnings over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods defined by HOUST and GDPC1, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production trend indicates expanding manufacturing output and economic activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with consecutive INDPRO increases, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation that may trigger premature monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle labor recovery regimes with strong non-farm payroll growth, S&P 500 forward returns turn positive as employment gains boost consumer spending and corporate earnings over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of early-cycle labor recovery periods defined by PAYEMS growth, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increase in housing starts and industrial production signals robust demand for goods alongside strong manufacturing output, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with concurrent HOUST and INDPRO increases, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.
